knowledge:
- key_parameters: responsedata=Matrix or data frame of multivariate response variables (Y) ;; predictdata=Matrix or data frame of predictor variables (X) ;; nlambda=Number of regularization parameters (lambda) to use for GGM estimation ;; ndist=Fine-tuning parameter based on the power of the adjacency matrix to infer the covariance structure ;; method=Method for precision matrix estimation; options are "glasso", "lasso", "mb", and "elastic" ;; PREC_for_graph=True precision matrix used for ROC evaluation in path_result_for_roc() ;; OMEGA_path=Array of estimated precision matrices across the lambda path ;; pathnumber=Number of lambda values in the path ;; result_assessment=Output from path_result_for_roc() used in plot_roc() ;; ith_lambda=Index of the lambda parameter to visualize in plotsngls()
- alternatives: method="glasso" uses graphical lasso (Yuan and Lin 2007; Friedman et al. 2007) ;; method="lasso" or method="mb" uses linear regression with lasso penalization (Meinshausen and Buhlmann 2006) ;; method="elastic" uses a combination of lasso (L1) and ridge (L2) regularization
- when_to_use: Use when analyzing multivariate Gaussian response data (e.g., high-throughput "omic" data) where response variables have a latent, sparse covariance structure, and you want to perform generalized least squares regression to estimate regression coefficients with improved accuracy and sandwich-estimated variances.
- pitfalls: Ensure the response data is multivariate Gaussian. The convertbeta() function requires the correct number of predictors q (including intercept if applicable, e.g., q+1 as shown in the example). Selecting ndist too small or too large can affect the covariance structure estimation; it is fine-tuned using the power of the adjacency matrix.

workflows.name: multivariate_gls_regression
workflows.intent: Perform multivariate GLS regression using GGM-based covariance estimation, convert coefficients to original scale, and select optimal parameters based on minimal variance or AIC/BIC.
workflows.stages: 1. Estimate precision and covariance matrices and fit GLS regression using sparsenetgls() ;; 2. Convert regression coefficients to original scale using convertbeta() ;; 3. Select optimal lambda and distance parameters using minimal variance of beta, AIC, or BIC ;; 4. Visualize the results using plotsngls()
workflows.code:
fitgls <- sparsenetgls(databand_Y, databand_X, nlambda=10, 
ndist=5, method="glasso")

#Convert the regression coefficients to its original scale
q <- dim(databand_X)[2]
nlambda=10

betagls <- matrix(nrow=nlambda, ncol=q+1)
for (i in seq_len(nlambda))   
betagls[i,] <- convertbeta(Y=databand_Y, X=databand_X, q=q+1,
beta0=fitgls$beta[,i])$betaconv

#Beta selection 

#select lamda and dist value based on the minimal variance of beta
ndist <- max(fitgls$power)-1
tr_gamma <- matrix(nrow=10, ncol=ndist-1)

for (j in seq_len(ndist-1))
    for (i in seq_len(nlambda)) 
        tr_gamma[i,j] <- (sum(diag(fitgls$covBeta[,,j,i]))) 

select.lambda.dist <- which(tr_gamma==min(tr_gamma), arr.ind=TRUE)
select.lambda.dist
betagls_select <- betagls[select.lambda.dist[1],]

#row is lambda and column is dist
varbeta <- diag(fitgls$covBeta[,,ndist,select.lambda.dist[1]])

##select lamda and dist value based on the AIC and BIC
select.lambda.dist2 <- which(fitgls$bic==min(fitgls$bic,na.rm=TRUE),
arr.ind=TRUE)
select.lambda.dist3 <- which(fitgls$aic==min(fitgls$aic,na.rm=TRUE),
arr.ind=TRUE)
varbeta_bic <- diag(fitgls$covBeta[,,ndist,select.lambda.dist2[1]])
varbeta_aic <- diag(fitgls$covBeta[,,ndist,select.lambda.dist3[1]])

plotsngls(fitgls,ith_lambda=5)

workflows.name: ggm_accuracy_assessment
workflows.intent: Assess the prediction accuracy of an estimated Gaussian Graphical Model (GGM) against a known true precision matrix.
workflows.stages: 1. Estimate precision matrices across a lambda path using sparsenetgls() ;; 2. Format the estimated precision matrices into a 3D array ;; 3. Calculate sensitivity, specificity, NPV, and PPV using path_result_for_roc() ;; 4. Plot the ROC curve using plot_roc()
workflows.code:
omega <- sparsenetgls(responsedata=databand_Y, predictdata=databand_X, 
nlambda=10, ndist=1, method="glasso")$PREC_seq
omega_est <- array(dim=c(50,50,10))
for (i in seq_len(10)) omega_est[,,i] <- as.matrix(omega[[i]])

roc_path_result <- path_result_for_roc(PREC_for_graph=prec, OMEGA_path=omega_est
, pathnumber=10)
plot_roc(result_assessment=roc_path_result, group=FALSE, ngroup=0,
est_names="glasso estimation")
